accepted.title: Degree distortion under algebraic Cremona embeddings
accepted.text: Let Crₙ(ℂ)=Bir(ℙⁿ_ℂ), with degree the common degree of homogeneous coordinate polynomials after canceling their common factor. Call Φ:Cr₂(ℂ)→Crₙ(ℂ) algebraic when its restriction to PGL₃(ℂ) is an algebraic family of birational maps. For every injective such homomorphism, is there C>0 depending only on Φ such that C⁻¹ deg(f)≤deg(Φ(f))≤C deg(f) for all f∈Cr₂(ℂ)?
accepted.subject: Algebraic Geometry & Birational Dynamics

locator.verified_from: Held PDF actual physical page and footer

accepted.scope_review: Source algebraic means restriction to PGL₃ is a morphism; it does not assume topological continuity on the whole Cremona group. Uniform C independent of f.
accepted.literature_finding: Author current works list includes later group-action and subgroup results; no universal distortion theorem located. Thesis establishes the dimension3 case, not every target dimension.

accepted.title: Intermediate degree growth for one birational map
accepted.text: For a smooth projective d-dimensional variety X over a field k with ample divisor H, define deg_H(f)=(f*H)·H^(d−1) for a birational self-map f. Does some such X,H,f have degree growth intermediate between polynomial and exponential? In particular, can deg_H(fⁿ)∼exp(√n) occur?

accepted.scope_review: One fixed birational self-map, not a finitely generated group maximum-degree sequence. The displayed exp√n clause is retained as the source example; no claim that it exhausts intermediate growth.
accepted.literature_finding: Current primary2016 degree-growth paper states Question1. Later author work on constraints and regularization does not supply intermediate single-map construction; fresh exact-intermediate-growth searches located no closure.

accepted.title: Dimension-only bound on finite polynomial degree exponents
accepted.text: For a smooth projective d-dimensional variety X over a field k with ample divisor H, define deg_H(f)=(f*H)·H^(d−1) for a birational self-map f. Put d_pol(f)=limsup_{n→∞} log(deg_H(fⁿ))/log n. For each d, does there exist a finite constant C(d), independent of k,X,H,f, such that d_pol(f)<C(d) whenever dimX=d and d_pol(f)<∞?
accepted.subject: Algebraic Geometry & Birational Dynamics

locator.verified_from: Held PDF actual physical page and footer

accepted.scope_review: Finite limsup exponent is the source definition, not an assumed exact polynomial asymptotic. All smooth projective varieties and fields; strict inequality as stated.
accepted.literature_finding: Primary2016 degree-growth Question5 poses this bound. The dimension3 exponent4 example is lower-bound evidence, not a disproof of a dimension-only bound. Current author works and fresh dpol/degree-growth searches found no universal closure.

accepted.title: Simple subgroups of small complex projective linear groups
accepted.text: Classify the abstract simple subgroups of PGL₂(ℂ) and PGL₃(ℂ), allowing infinitely generated subgroups. Beyond finite simple subgroups and PSL₂(k) for subfields k⊆ℂ in the dimension2 case, which other simple groups occur?
accepted.subject: Algebraic Geometry & Birational Dynamics

accepted.scope_review: Abstract simple subgroups, not merely closed algebraic subgroups or finite subgroups. No finite-generation assumption: finitely generated simple linear groups are finite.
accepted.literature_finding: Urech2018/2020 simple-Cremona paper reduces its dimension2 birational problem to simple subgroups of PGL₃; this is not a classification of all abstract simple linear subgroups. Current author list and fresh PSL/simple-subgroup searches located no full answer.

accepted.title: Residual finiteness of finitely generated plane Cremona subgroups
accepted.text: Does Cr₂(ℂ)=Bir(ℙ²_ℂ) have the Malcev property: for every finitely generated subgroup Γ≤Cr₂(ℂ) and every nonidentity γ∈Γ, is there a homomorphism Γ→Q to a finite group Q in which γ has nonidentity image?
accepted.subject: Algebraic Geometry & Birational Dynamics

locator.verified_from: Held PDF actual physical page and footer

accepted.scope_review: Residual finiteness of every finitely generated subgroup; not residual finiteness of the entire Cremona group. Source proves only that its finitely generated simple subgroups are finite.
accepted.literature_finding: Author current list and fresh Cremona/Malcev/residual-finiteness searches found no all-subgroup theorem or counterexample. Finite/simple subgroup and elliptic-boundedness results do not settle arbitraryΓ.
